primary_action.input: Tab to Proof B, Enter; Tab to Right, Enter; Tab to Check this proof, Enter
primary_action.expected: Show the difference between the marks and reject Proof B
primary_action.observed: The left mark showed aligned inks; the right showed red below blue. The check reported that the proof was rotated.

A-1440.edge_observation: Proof C showed aligned inks at both marks and returned 'Ready to print' when checked.
A-1440.fact_check: The visible mark positions support the stated left/right difference. The rotation diagnosis is presented by the interface; its physical cause was not independently verified.
A-1440.strength: The large, textured sheet, condensed blue lettering, red disc and sweeping ink bands create a coherent print-workshop composition. Keyboard focus and the result are visible.
A-1440.weakness: Comparing ends requires switching the enlarged mark and remembering the previous one. The lower bands cross the small poster caption, and the artwork feels more like a familiar concert poster than a singular museum identity.
A-1440.repair: Show both enlarged marks together and give the lower caption clear space; develop a more distinctive visual motif tied to the workshop.

primary_action.input: Tab and Enter to select Proof B, inspect Right, then activate Check this proof
primary_action.expected: Reject the mismatched proof with the relevant mark visible
primary_action.observed: The right mark showed red below blue, and the rejection explained that the left mark aligned.

A-390.edge_observation: Proof C passed with both marks aligned. Scrolling exposed the full poster while the selected proof and result remained visible.
A-390.fact_check: The result matches the inspected marks; the physical rotation diagnosis is not independently verified.
A-390.strength: The task appears before the artwork, with readable controls, a clear focus ring and a compact full-sheet view after a short scroll.
A-390.weakness: The one-at-a-time mark control makes comparison dependent on memory; the poster's small supporting copy is difficult to read at phone scale.
A-390.repair: Place both mark diagrams side by side and enlarge or simplify the poster's supporting text.

primary_action.input: Tab to Proof B and press Enter; Tab to Check this proof and press Enter
primary_action.expected: Compare both ends and reject Proof B
primary_action.observed: Both diagrams appeared together: left aligned, right red below blue. The check reported the proof rotated.

B-1440.edge_observation: Selecting and checking Proof C showed both marks aligned and returned 'Ready to print.'
B-1440.fact_check: The displayed diagrams support the alignment result. The physical cause described as rotation was not independently verified.
B-1440.strength: Both ends are immediately comparable, and the poster's bold type, registration marks, red disc and layered curves connect the task to the sheet.
B-1440.weakness: The small caption collides visually with the lower curves. The concert-poster language is appealing but does not yet feel unmistakably specific enough for a museum landing page.
B-1440.repair: Protect the caption's space and develop a more distinctive workshop-specific visual signature while preserving the side-by-side comparison.

primary_action.input: Tab and Enter to select Proof B, then Tab to Check this proof and press Enter
primary_action.expected: See both marks and reject the proof
primary_action.observed: The side-by-side diagrams showed the left aligned and the right red diamond below its cross; the rejection appeared below the focused button.

B-390.edge_observation: Proof C passed with both diagrams aligned. A short scroll showed the entire poster alongside the selected proof, diagrams and ready result.
B-390.fact_check: The displayed diagrams support the alignment result. The physical rotation diagnosis was not independently verified.
B-390.strength: The two diagrams remain legible together at phone width, reducing steps and memory load while keeping the main task and sheet in view.
B-390.weakness: The full poster's supporting text is tiny, and the curved bands crowd its lower caption; the visual identity remains closer to a generic gig poster than a distinctive museum destination.
B-390.repair: Increase the supporting type's effective size and separate it from the curves; retain the paired diagrams.

preference.reason: Both versions share the same strong poster and working keyboard outcomes, but B makes the essential left-to-right comparison immediate at both widths and requires fewer keyboard steps. Neither artwork is yet sufficiently distinctive, in this review, to anchor a memorable museum landing page on its own.

studies.revision: Separate caption and intersect ink plates

primary_action.input: Tab twice, Enter on Proof B; Tab twice, Enter on Check this proof.
primary_action.expected: Select Proof B, compare its marks, and reject it.
primary_action.observed: Proof B selected. The left mark aligned and the right red diamond sat below the blue cross. Checking reported that the proof was rotated and described the mismatch.

A-1440.edge_observation: Shift+Tab and Enter selected Proof C; Tab and Enter checked it. Both marks aligned and the status said it was ready to print.
A-1440.fact_check: The visible marks and the rejection and success messages agree. The rotation explanation is presented by the interface; its physical cause cannot be independently verified from this review.
A-1440.strength: The full sheet gives the workshop a strong identity: a condensed Night Machine title, intersecting red arcs and pale wave lines make a memorable concert-poster image. The paired mark diagrams make comparison immediate.
A-1440.weakness: The poster's dense central graphic competes somewhat with the registration lesson, and the marks in the comparison panels are small.
A-1440.repair: Enlarge the comparison marks slightly while preserving the paired layout and the poster's intersecting-wave focal point.

primary_action.input: Tab twice, Enter on Proof B; Tab twice, Enter on Check this proof.
primary_action.expected: Reject the proof with a mismatch at one end.
primary_action.observed: The side-by-side diagrams showed the left aligned and the right red diamond below the blue cross; the rejection appeared under the focused button.

A-390.edge_observation: Keyboard selection and checking of Proof C produced the ready-to-print message and two aligned diagrams.
A-390.fact_check: The visible diagrams support both messages. The poster is almost entirely visible alongside the task evidence, but the review tool did not accept the attempted PageDown key, so a deliberate scroll to inspect its bottom edge was not verified.
A-390.strength: The two ends remain side by side at phone width, and the compact poster retains the distinctive crossing waves and title.
A-390.weakness: The poster and its corner marks are small on the phone; the bottom edge is at the viewport boundary in the captured result.
A-390.repair: Provide a deliberate enlarged sheet view or zoom control while retaining access to the side-by-side mark comparison.

primary_action.input: Tab twice, Enter on Proof B; Tab twice, Enter on Check this proof.
primary_action.expected: Select and reject the mismatched proof.
primary_action.observed: The left mark aligned, the right red diamond fell below the blue cross, and the status explained the rejection.

B-1440.edge_observation: Proof C selected and checked from the keyboard; both marks aligned and the ready-to-print status appeared.
B-1440.fact_check: The visible marks agree with the result messages. The stated physical rotation is not independently verified.
B-1440.strength: The oversized title and isolated red disc give the sheet clear hierarchy; the task panel provides a direct, labeled comparison of both ends.
B-1440.weakness: The lower arcs cross the small 'One set after dark' line and crowd the frame. The separated disc and arcs feel less integrated into a distinctive poster identity than A's intersecting composition.
B-1440.repair: Reposition the lower caption and resolve the arcs at the frame edge; connect the disc and line work into a more recognizable visual idea.

primary_action.input: Tab twice, Enter on Proof B; Tab twice, Enter on Check this proof.
primary_action.expected: Show and explain the failed registration.
primary_action.observed: The paired diagrams and rejection message exposed the aligned left mark and low right red diamond.

B-390.edge_observation: Proof C checked successfully, with both marks labeled aligned and a ready-to-print message.
B-390.fact_check: The diagrams support the displayed outcomes. The review tool rejected the attempted End key, so a deliberate scroll to inspect the poster's bottom edge was not verified.
B-390.strength: The main task and both mark diagrams remain visible together; the large title survives reduction well.
B-390.weakness: At phone scale the lower caption becomes tiny and is crossed by the arcs, weakening the full-sheet composition and its museum-landing-page identity.
B-390.repair: Separate the caption from the arcs and simplify or enlarge the lower poster detail for small screens.

preference.reason: Both views performed the keyboard task equally well in the observed flows. A's intertwined red and pale waveforms create a more cohesive, memorable poster, while B's lower arcs collide with its caption. Neither view was verified through the requested deliberate phone scroll because the attempted scrolling keys were rejected by the review tool.

primary_action.input: Tab to Proof B, Enter; Tab to Check this proof, Enter.
primary_action.expected: Show both registration marks and reject the misregistered proof.
primary_action.observed: Proof B selected. The left inks aligned; the right red diamond sat below the blue cross. The check reported that the proof was rotated.

A-1440.edge_observation: Proof C showed both marks aligned and returned 'Ready to print' after keyboard activation. Focus remained visibly outlined on the check button.
A-1440.fact_check: The visible marks and result agree for B and C. The rotation diagnosis is presented by the interface; the screenshots alone do not establish the physical cause.
A-1440.strength: Large, adjacent mark diagrams with plain-language descriptions make comparing the ends quick. The full sheet combines condensed type, crossing red bands, blue waves, and a registration target into a memorable print-shop identity.
A-1440.weakness: The large labels on the sheet compete slightly with the poster itself, and the workshop context is otherwise quite sparse for a museum landing page.
A-1440.repair: Keep the enlarged comparison panel, but reduce the sheet labels' prominence and add a concise editorial context for the workshop.

primary_action.input: Tab to Proof B, Enter; Tab to Check this proof, Enter.
primary_action.expected: Compare both ends and receive the rejection.
primary_action.observed: Both enlarged diagrams remained side by side; the left aligned and the right red diamond was below the cross. The rejection appeared immediately below the focused button.

A-390.edge_observation: Proof C produced two aligned diagrams and the ready-to-print message. The poster extended below the initial viewport; a complete full-sheet view was not verified with the available keyboard scrolling attempt.
A-390.fact_check: The visible descriptions match the diagrams. The full poster's bottom edge is clipped in the saved task-state captures, so its complete phone presentation remains unverified.
A-390.strength: The task, comparison, and result stay together above the poster. The enlarged marks remain easy to distinguish on a narrow screen.
A-390.weakness: The small poster labels and reduced artwork lose some of the desktop sheet's impact; the complete sheet was not captured.
A-390.repair: Preserve the side-by-side enlarged marks and ensure the entire sheet can be comfortably inspected below the result, with a clear visual transition to it.

primary_action.input: Tab to Proof B, Enter; Tab to Check this proof, Enter.
primary_action.expected: Show the differing marks and reject the proof.
primary_action.observed: The left mark aligned, the right diamond was below its cross, and the check reported a rotated proof.

B-1440.edge_observation: Selecting Proof C and checking it returned 'Ready to print' with both diagrams aligned.
B-1440.fact_check: The visible marks support the alignment statements. The stated physical cause of rotation is interface feedback, not independently verified.
B-1440.strength: The uncluttered sheet gives the Night Machine artwork room to dominate. Its bold condensed lettering and intersecting waveforms provide a recognizable editorial focal point.
B-1440.weakness: The comparison diagrams are small relative to their panels, making the fine offset harder to inspect than in A. The artwork is distinctive, but the surrounding workshop identity is thin for a museum landing page.
B-1440.repair: Enlarge both diagrams while retaining the clean sheet, and develop the workshop's editorial context around the poster.

primary_action.input: Tab to Proof B, Enter; Tab to Check this proof, Enter.
primary_action.expected: Compare the ends and receive the rejection.
primary_action.observed: Both mark descriptions and diagrams updated; the right red diamond was below the cross. The rejection appeared beneath the focused button.

B-390.edge_observation: Proof C returned the ready-to-print message. The edge capture shows the full poster and the task result together after keyboard scrolling.
B-390.fact_check: The result and visible mark descriptions agree. The poster's corner marks are very small at this width, so the larger comparison panel carries the task.
B-390.strength: The full poster and result fit together in the final view, preserving the relationship between the decision and the artwork.
B-390.weakness: The comparison marks are tiny on the phone, especially the aligned diamond, even though the text explains each state.
B-390.repair: Increase the mark diagrams and their line weight, preserving the two-column comparison and descriptive text.

preference.reason: Both complete the keyboard task and share a strong poster identity, but A's larger diagrams make the crucial left-versus-right comparison substantially easier at both widths. B presents a cleaner full sheet, particularly on the phone, but its small marks weaken the central task.

primary_action.input: Tab to Proof B, Enter; Tab to Check this proof, Enter.
primary_action.expected: Show both marks and reject the misregistered proof.
primary_action.observed: The left mark aligned; the right red diamond fell below the blue cross. The check reported the rotation and identified the right mark.

A-1440.edge_observation: Proof C showed aligned marks and returned Ready to print. Enter on the plate control switched its status to Blue impression only and back; Proof C and its result remained selected.
A-1440.fact_check: The enlarged marks and rejection text agree. The lift state was reported by the control, but its desktop artwork was not separately captured.
A-1440.strength: Large side-by-side mark diagrams make the comparison immediate. The condensed title and red arcs crossing blue waves give the concert poster a recognizable graphic identity.
A-1440.weakness: The plate toolbar pushes the bottom of the sheet below the initial desktop viewport. The interface feels like a useful workshop exercise more than a fully developed museum landing page.
A-1440.repair: Preserve the plate interaction while fitting the complete sheet into the desktop composition, and add more editorial context around the workshop without competing with the proof task.

primary_action.input: Tab and Enter to select Proof B and activate Check this proof.
primary_action.expected: Expose the difference between both marks and reject B.
primary_action.observed: Both enlarged marks remained side by side; the left aligned and the right red diamond sat below the cross. The rejection explained the difference.

A-390.edge_observation: Proof C returned Ready to print. Lifting the red plate visibly removed the red poster elements while the blue waves and Proof C remained; a second Enter restored the red artwork.
A-390.fact_check: The full poster was not verified by scrolling: PageDown did not visibly move the page and End was rejected by the review tool. The captured phone views show the task evidence and most, but not the bottom, of the sheet.
A-390.strength: The task, comparison, feedback, and top of the poster fit together on the phone; text labels reinforce the color-coded marks.
A-390.weakness: The toolbar consumes valuable vertical space, leaving the lower poster out of view in the captured state. The tiny marks on the sheet itself are much harder to inspect than the enlarged diagrams.
A-390.repair: Make the plate control more compact and ensure a straightforward scroll path to the complete sheet while retaining access to the proof result.

primary_action.input: Tab to Proof B, Enter; Tab to Check this proof, Enter.
primary_action.expected: Show the two marks and reject the misregistered proof.
primary_action.observed: The left mark aligned and the right red diamond fell below the blue cross; the check explained the rotation.

B-1440.edge_observation: Proof C showed alignment at both ends and returned Ready to print. No red-plate control was present.
B-1440.fact_check: The visible marks support the rejection and ready result. No claim about plate lifting is supported for this view.
B-1440.strength: The entire lavender sheet, including its lower registration marks, fits in the desktop view. Its heavy lettering and intersecting wave and arc forms make a memorable poster.
B-1440.weakness: The sheet and task panel are visually clear but the surrounding workshop editorial identity is sparse; the graphic alone does not establish a rich museum context.
B-1440.repair: Add concise curatorial or process context while keeping the full sheet and the comparison panel visible together.

primary_action.input: Tab and Enter to select Proof B and activate Check this proof.
primary_action.expected: Compare both ends and reject B.
primary_action.observed: The side-by-side diagrams showed the left aligned and the right red diamond below blue. The rejection named the discrepancy.

B-390.edge_observation: Proof C aligned at both ends and returned Ready to print. No red-plate control was present.
B-390.fact_check: The poster is nearly complete in the initial phone capture, but its bottom edge is clipped. A scrolled full-sheet view was not verified.
B-390.strength: The compact poster remains largely visible beneath the task and result, and the enlarged comparison avoids relying on the tiny marks on the artwork.
B-390.weakness: The poster's bottom edge is clipped in the captured viewport, and the surrounding page gives the artwork little curatorial context.
B-390.repair: Provide a verified scroll position that shows the full sheet, and add a short workshop context that does not displace the task.

preference.reason: Both designs make comparison and keyboard checking clear and share the same strong poster. A's working plate lift adds a meaningful way to understand the two-color print while preserving the selected proof. B fits more of the sheet on screen, which A should recover.
